name: United Noodles
neighborhoodOrCity: Seward, Minneapolis (2015 E. 24th St.) and Woodbury (7730 Hudson Rd., Suite 60)
whatItIs: Pan-Asian grocery founded in 1972 by Ramon Tan, an immigrant from the Philippines; a 2020 article named Annie Dingle and Eric Fung as co-owners. Not a Filipino specialty store today.
evidence: Own site lists both stores and current products; page metadata shows it was modified Oct. 28, 2026. Founding history from Minnesota Daily, Feb. 6, 2020 (https://mndaily.com/arts-entertainment/aegrocery/02/06/2020/snoadmin/).

name: Lumpia City
neighborhoodOrCity: Minnesota State Fairgrounds, Falcon Heights (west side of Liggett St. between Carnes and Judson avenues)
whatItIs: Filipino-style lumpia stand; debuted in 2025 with pizza lumpia and ube butter banana French toast lumpia.
evidence: FOX 9's list of new 2026 State Fair foods includes Lumpia City's Longanisa Cheese Curd Lumpia with its 2026 location. Seasonal vendor; operates during the fair.

name: Philippine Center of Minnesota
whatItIs: Community center opened in 2009 by the Fil-Minnesotan Association; hosts gatherings and Philippine consular outreach.
evidence: Philippine Consulate General in Chicago press release dated Nov. 17, 2025 reports a one-day outreach held at the center, organized with the Philippine Center of Minnesota and the Fil-Minnesotan Association.

name: Filipino Village Grocery Store
neighborhoodOrCity: Mounds View (2408 County Road I area, next to Kusina)
whatItIs: Filipino grocery opened in November 2020 by Herman and Faith Rott, selling malunggay, puto cheese, pan de sal, pichi-pichi and chorizo de Cebu.
evidence: Sahan Journal profile dated Jan. 28, 2022. Kusina's site still describes itself as next door to the grocery but shows no date. No dated 2025 or 2026 evidence found.

name: Kusina, A Pinoy Turo Turo
neighborhoodOrCity: Mounds View (2408 County Road I, at Edgewood)
whatItIs: Walk-up, point-and-choose Filipino restaurant; name means 'kitchen' in Cebuano. Chef-owner Jailin Tabares also ran Inday's Kitchen food truck (2023).
evidence: Own site describes the restaurant and location but shows no hours or dated content. Chef appeared on a Macalester panel Oct. 19, 2023 (The Mac Weekly).

name: Ku•ma•in
whatItIs: Filipino takeout started as a Brooklyn Park pop-up by Josie Schuette; name means 'eat' in Tagalog.
evidence: CCX Media opening story is undated on the opened page; no 2025 or 2026 evidence found.

name: Taste of the Philippines
neighborhoodOrCity: Downtown Rochester (First Avenue Food Court, skyway level)
whatItIs: Rochester's first Filipino restaurant, opened Nov. 1, 2023 by owner Irene Mills; adobo, pancit, halo-halo, lumpia, cassava cake.
evidence: Downtown Rochester listing is undated; KTTC opening story dated Dec. 6, 2023. No 2025 or 2026 evidence found.

name: Apoy
whatItIs: Filipino restaurant founded by Curt Rademacher, Shawn Nafstad and Sherwin Resurreccion.
evidence: Mpls.St.Paul Magazine review is not dated on the opened page; apoympls.com returned no readable content. No 2025 or 2026 evidence found.

name: Pinoy Fusion
whatItIs: Filipino-Chinese fusion food truck (lumpia, sisig, lechon kawali, cassava cake).
evidence: Catering listing is undated; named as a newer Filipino business at a 2023 Macalester panel.

name: Phil-Oriental
neighborhoodOrCity: Frogtown / University Avenue, St. Paul (789 University Ave. W., per 2013 report)
whatItIs: Older Asian grocery that a 2013 MPR guest called the only source she knew for Filipino ingredients.
evidence: Only source is MPR News, Sept. 25, 2013; 'Phil Oriental Imports' was named at a 2023 Macalester panel. No current evidence found.

name: Manila Sizzling Wok and Grill
whatItIs: Carinderia-style Filipino eatery whose proprietor, Rowan Gutierrez, spoke at a 2023 Macalester panel.
evidence: Named only in The Mac Weekly, Nov. 2023; no address or current listing found.

name: Subo
whatItIs: Described as the city's first Filipino-focused restaurant, opened 2009.
evidence: Mpls.St.Paul Magazine says the restaurant 'didn't last more than a year.'
